title: Cambodia and Thailand Open UN-Backed Maritime Conciliation in Singapore
detail: Foreign ministers of Cambodia and Thailand delivered opening statements in Singapore at the first meeting of a UNCLOS Annex V Conciliation Commission over their overlapping maritime claims in the Gulf of Thailand -- a roughly 26,000 sq km area believed to hold about 12 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and oil worth an estimated $300 billion. The three-day session (Sept 14-16) follows Cambodia's June move to trigger compulsory conciliation after Thailand terminated the 2001 MOU that had governed maritime talks for 25 years. Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn said Cambodia is seeking a single all-purpose maritime boundary treaty, or alternatively a joint development and resource-sharing arrangement, while Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said the proceedings are limited to maritime boundary delimitation. The five-member commission, chaired by Australian diplomat Katrina Cooper, has roughly 12 months to draft compromise proposals; the process is non-binding.

media.caption: Cambodia and Thailand open UNCLOS Annex V conciliation proceedings over Gulf of Thailand maritime claims

title: Cambodia Protests Thai Trench Construction Near Boundary Pillar No. 9
detail: The Royal Government of Cambodia lodged a formal protest after Thai armed forces reportedly used heavy machinery on September 15 to level ground and dig an earthen trench near Boundary Pillar No. 9 in the Ta Tum area of Anlong Veng district, Oddar Meanchey province. Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation said the activity violated its sovereignty and territorial integrity as delimited by the 1:200,000-scale Franco-Siamese Convention maps of 1904 and the 1907 Treaty, and breached Article 5 of the June 14, 2000 MOU on Survey and Demarcation of the Land Boundary. Cambodia demanded Thailand cease the work and honor its Dec 27, 2025 GBC commitments to de-escalate and refer boundary work to the Joint Boundary Commission. Thailand had not issued a public response to this specific incident as of this update; the episode follows earlier Thai road-construction activity reported between the same pillars in mid-July 2026.

media.caption: Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs protests reported Thai trench construction near Boundary Pillar No. 9, Ta Tum area, Anlong Veng district
